subject.title: [Feature]: Support external unified session storage for stateless session mode

question: Should OpenClaw support external shared session storage as a core storage backend, a plugin/API extension point, or an external deployment pattern after the SQLite/accessor work settles?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but backend ownership, credentials, consistency semantics, transcript lifecycle, migration behavior, and config shape are product and architecture decisions.

options.title: Design a storage contract after the SQLite seam
options.body: Define a backend-neutral contract covering session metadata, transcript events, migrations, pruning, credentials, consistency, tests, and docs before selecting Redis, Mongo, Postgres, or plugin ownership.

options.title: Keep this external/plugin-only
options.body: Document sticky sessions or external orchestration as deployment guidance and pursue plugin/API gaps only if current plugin surfaces cannot express the storage backend safely.

options.title: Fold into broader database abstraction
options.body: Treat external session storage as a subset of the broader networked database backend effort and keep this issue as a linked session-specific requirements source.

recommendation.title: Design a storage contract after the SQLite seam
recommendation.body: Define a backend-neutral contract covering session metadata, transcript events, migrations, pruning, credentials, consistency, tests, and docs before selecting Redis, Mongo, Postgres, or plugin ownership.

likelyOwner.reason: The current session/transcript storage boundary and migration tracker are the closest prerequisite design surface for this choice.
